quest.title: The Search for a Physician
quest.description: Someone seems to be asking for help outside Bubu Pharmacy...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x550, Mora x31125, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x7

dialogues.speaker: Herbalist Gui
dialogues.text: ...What's your name, buddy? Are you here to buy some medicine? Where are your mom and dad?

dialogues.speaker: Qiqi
dialogues.text: Are you lost?

dialogues.speaker: Ayu
dialogues.text: No, I'm not! Um, my name's Ayu, and I'm here because—

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey there, Qiqi! Hi, Gui! What's going on?

dialogues.speaker: Qiqi
dialogues.text: #Hi, {NICKNAME} and Paimon...

dialogues.speaker: Herbalist Gui
dialogues.text: Ah, you've actually come at a perfect time! This little boy seems to have gotten himself lost. I think he must be new to the city. Probably wandered away from his parents, and—

dialogues.speaker: Ayu
dialogues.text: No, listen to me! I'm not the one who's lost. It's my dad!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Your dad? How does a fully grown man manage to get lost in Liyue Harbor?

dialogues.speaker: Ayu
dialogues.text: Well... My dad's always been kinda forgetful. In the past, he was just a little slow to react sometimes, but I'm worried that it's getting more serious.

dialogues.speaker: Qiqi
dialogues.text: So... What about your mom?

dialogues.speaker: Ayu
dialogues.text: She went out a few days ago to gather some herbs for my dad, but she still hasn't come back... Meanwhile, my dad's been getting worse and worse.

dialogues.speaker: Ayu
dialogues.text: I remembered that the owner of Bubu Pharmacy always runs a clinic in Qingce Village during the Lantern Rite. So I thought, why don't I take Dad to Liyue Harbor to see him there...

response.speaker: Ayu
response.text: When we got to the city gate, I took a moment to ask the Millelith guards for directions to the pharmacy... and then when I turned back around, my dad was gone!

response.speaker: Ayu
response.text: I asked the Millelith guys to go find him, but he said they won't be able to send that many people. So then I figured, maybe I could ask some other people in the city to help...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #You came to the right place! We're pros at finding people! Isn't that right, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It'll be a piece of cake for us.

response.speaker: Qiqi
response.text: Changsheng can help. She has a good sense of smell, like a dog.

response.speaker: Changsheng
response.text: Hey! Who's talking about me behind my back?

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: Changsheng, Qiqi meant that as a compliment. There's no need to be upset.

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: Hello, child. You mentioned that you were looking for the owner of Bubu Pharmacy. How might we be of service?

response.speaker: Ayu
response.text: You have a talking snake...? Oh! A—Are you Uncle Baizhu?

response.speaker: Changsheng
response.text: Pfft! "Uncle" Baizhu...

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: ...Changsheng, now's not the time.

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: My dear boy, could you tell me more about your father's condition? As much as you can recall.

response.speaker: Ayu
response.text: Yes, Unc— ...Dr. Baizhu.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Ayu explains his father's health situation to Baizhu...

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: I see... And your family lives near Qingce Village, you say? I visit patients there frequently, but I don't recall ever seeing you or your parents.

response.speaker: Ayu
response.text: Uh-huh... My mom doesn't like meeting other people, especially during Lantern Rite. She always tells me to just stay at home and keep my dad company.

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: ...Is that so.

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: Ayu, by any chance... is your mother's name Jiangli?

response.speaker: Ayu
response.text: Whoa! Yeah, it is! Do you know my mom, Dr. Baizhu?

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: I certainly do... Gui, Qiqi, are there any pressing matters in the pharmacy at the moment?

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: Ayu's parents are old acquaintances of mine, so I would very much like to assist with the search... Would the two of you have time to join me?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Don't forget us two! We already told Ayu that we'd help!

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: Oh really? Well, that's wonderful. We are most grateful for your support.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You can count on us.

response.speaker: Herbalist Gui
response.text: Qiqi and I need to clear up the shop front first, but once that's taken care of, we'll be right out to help you with the search!

response.speaker: Qiqi
response.text: Family is... very important.

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: Thank you. Then I'll leave you to handle the pharmacy.

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, why don't you come with me and Ayu? Let's start by talking to the Millelith guards at the city gates, see if they have an update.

talks.objective: Ask the Millelith guards outside Liyue Harbor

dialogues.speaker: Cai Le
dialogues.text: ...They searched to the north, but couldn't find anyone who matched the description.

dialogues.speaker: Cai Xun
dialogues.text: Ugh, well that complicates things. The city folks say there's no sign of him, either. We need to start looking further afield... but where are we gonna get the people?

dialogues.speaker: Ayu
dialogues.text: Excuse me, Sirs! Have you found out anything about my dad yet?

dialogues.speaker: Cai Xun
dialogues.text: Ah, hey there, buddy... Dr. Baizhu? What brings you out this way?

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: The boy asked for our help, so we're here to join the search. Any new developments to update us on?

dialogues.speaker: Cai Xun
dialogues.text: Thank goodness! We were just discussing how we're running out of manpower.

dialogues.speaker: Cai Xun
dialogues.text: As for updates... I'm sorry to say that we've searched the surrounding area thoroughly, but didn't find anything.

dialogues.speaker: Cai Le
dialogues.text: The guards at the crossing up ahead said they hadn't seen anyone, either, so we don't believe he was heading towards the Guili Plains... But it is possible that he was bound for Luhua Pool.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: Luhua Pool... The terrain there can be tricky to navigate. Let's hope he hasn't run into any trouble.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We'll take that area.

dialogues.speaker: Cai Xun
dialogues.text: You will? Great, we can't thank you enough!

dialogues.speaker: Cai Le
dialogues.text: Sorry we weren't able to find your dad, buddy.

dialogues.speaker: Ayu
dialogues.text: That's okay. Thank you for trying!

talks.objective: Search the area near Luhua Pool

dialogues.speaker: Herbalist Gui
dialogues.text: Can you believe that little boy brought his father all this way to see the doctor? What a remarkable child.

dialogues.speaker: Herbalist Gui
dialogues.text: I didn't even know how to buy medicine by myself when I was his age.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh no! It's... Hey, you! Stop, don't go any further...!
Watch where you're going!
...Ugh!

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Dear customer, Wangsheng Funeral Parlor does appreciate your patronage, but you needn't hasten the inevitable! Are you alright?
Ugh... Urgh...

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: ...Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Ayu
dialogues.text: Dad!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Hu Tao!

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: #My, my, who do we have here? Mm-hmm! It's {NICKNAME} and Paimon! And...

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: ...Ugh. My worst nightmare.

dialogues.speaker: Changsheng
dialogues.text: Hah. I see she still hasn't warmed to you.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: Hehe, thank you, Director Hu, for saving this man.

dialogues.speaker: Ayu
dialogues.text: Dad, are you okay? Do you recognize me? It's me, Ayu!
You're... Ayu? Uh... who am I...?

dialogues.speaker: Ayu
dialogues.text: Your name is Jialiang, and you live just west of Qingce Village. You were supposed to come to Liyue Harbor to see the doctor... Remember? Does that jog your memory?

dialogues.speaker: Jialiang
dialogues.text: My name is Jialiang... Liyue Harbor, see the doctor... Yes, yes, I'm Jialiang, and I need to see the doctor... Wait, why do I need to see the doctor...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh-oh, he seems in really bad shape! We need to get him back to Bubu Pharmacy right away!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sorry, Hu Tao, gotta dash. Dinner's on us next time!

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Hold on a second.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: You're not seriously thinking of taking him to Bubu Pharmacy in this state, are you?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Why not, what's the problem?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Come on, Baizhu, don't tell me you haven't noticed it? Didn't your master teach you how to spot the signs?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Why do I get the sense that you spotted them right away... but you're planning to use it for your own ends?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Use what? What are you talking about? Paimon's lost...

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: ...There are traces of god remains in Jialiang's system.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Yes, but more importantly, they're on the verge of an outburst. If that happens, the consequences will be unthinkable.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's sorry, what!?

dialogues.speaker: Jialiang
dialogues.text: G—God... remains...?

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: ...There's no need to worry, Director Hu. I have methods of keeping them at bay.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: It is the sworn duty of all who practice medicine to cure illnesses and save lives. What reason would I have to neglect a patient in need who is right there in front of me?

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: Besides... it was my late master's dying wish to be able to save this patient in particular. Perhaps, out of respect for him, you could give me a day's grace so that I have time to treat him?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Now you're bringing my great-uncle into this? Baizhu... Just what are you planning this time?

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: Merely to cure this man, nothing more. But of course, if you have any doubt as to my intentions, you are more than welcome to accompany me to Bubu Pharmacy, and monitor my activities.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Oh really? I thought I was persona non grata at Bubu Pharmacy? You're being unusually generous today.

choices.text: Don't forget that we're here, too.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: ...Okay, deal. We're not gonna solve anything by keeping Jialiang here.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: #I'm happy to do it your way but... only for my great-uncle's sake. And {NICKNAME}'s, of course.

response.speaker: Changsheng
response.text: #You must be pleased you brought {NICKNAME} along. Otherwise, this would've been a much more vexing ordeal.

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: ...Well, time is of the essence. Let's get ourselves back to Bubu Pharmacy at once.

choices.text: We won't let things get out of hand.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: ...Blockages within the cardiovascular system... reduced blood flow and energy circulation...

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: I see. I suppose this must have caused the cognitive abnormalities.

dialogues.speaker: Ayu
dialogues.text: Dr. Baizhu... How bad is it? Can you cure him?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Don't you worry, Baizhu's a really great doctor. He's sure to find a way! Isn't that right, Baizhu?

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: ...Ayu, do you know when your father first started displaying these symptoms?

dialogues.speaker: Ayu
dialogues.text: Um... I'm not sure. He's been like this for as long as I can remember, but it wasn't as bad as this when I was still little...

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: Hmm, so it's been a long time indeed...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is it a grim prognosis...?

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: ...No, I have a treatment plan in mind. We can start tonight.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: Come and see me again tomorrow morning. I promise that by then, Ayu will find his father healthy and lucid again.

dialogues.speaker: Ayu
dialogues.text: Thank you, Dr. Baizhu, thank you so much!

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: If you still have any misgivings, Director Hu, please feel free to hang around for as long as you wish.

dialogues.speaker: Changsheng
dialogues.text: However, it would be best if you step outside this room. A doctor must be able to focus when treating a patient. Any distractions heighten the risk of complications.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Yes, of course, absolutely, I'll just go and look at the flowers, or something... But I will be back in an instant at the first sign that something's amiss.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We'll be heading out now, too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: See you tomorrow, Baizhu and Changsheng!

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: Bye for now, everyone.

dialogues.speaker: Changsheng
dialogues.text: ...Are you ready, Baizhu?

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: ...Ready as I'll ever be — I'm used to it by now. Come on, let's get started.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Phew... All's well that ends well, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Y'know, Paimon's kind of curious after hearing Baizhu mention those people from his past... What do you think they were like?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! You must be curious too, right? Let's go see what we can find out while Baizhu's busy treating Ayu's dad!

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: While I'm idling time on admiring the scenery, the spectacled snake-bedecked doc's doing surgery...

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Hello, you busy bees. And what do you have to discuss with the Funeral Director today?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Um, so...

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Actually, don't tell me — let me guess! Hmm... From the looks on your faces, you've got some questions for me?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ehehe... guilty as charged! So, um, we were just a little curious about Baizhu's Master. What was he like?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, and also — how come you and Baizhu could tell so quickly that Jialiang had god remains in his system?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Huh? I thought I told you once before? Wangsheng Funeral Parlor was first founded to fight back against the vengeful wrath of gods defeated in war.

choices.text: Oh, that vaguely rings a bell...

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Hah. Well, it is a dusty old tale by this point. Long story short: In the ancient world, dead gods were acting up, so our ancestors started purifying the air and burning the bodies of the deceased to guard the border between life and death...

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: These days, we don't deal with the wrath of the gods anymore, but all the relevant know-how is still passed down to each generation. So we can identify gods' remains when we see them.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, Paimon gets it now. ...Wait, so how did Baizhu learn to spot them?

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Almost certainly from his master — who was also my great-uncle. Baizhu's master was my grandpa's younger brother, a former deputy director of Wangsheng Funeral Parlor.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow, fancy that! Huh... So, if he was from Wangsheng Funeral Parlor, how'd he end up as Baizhu's Master?

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: According to my grandpa, he and my great-uncle once went traveling together when they were young. They ended up at Chenyu Vale, where they met a pharmacist.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: That pharmacist must've cast some sort of spell on my great-uncle, because after that encounter, he suddenly announced he wanted to leave the family business and go practice medicine instead.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: My grandpa had a huge argument with him, but he couldn't convince him to stay.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: So my grandpa inherited the Funeral Parlor, while my great-uncle stayed in Chenyu Vale to practice medicine... They never spoke to each other again.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Funeral director to doctor is a pretty big career change. Kinda hard to imagine... But why did it drive a wedge between them for the rest of their lives? That seems a bit extreme.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: If he had just become a regular doctor, there would have been no issue. After all, the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor wasn't unlike a regular doctor's clinic in the early days.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: But according to my grandpa, the pharmacist they met had a very ominous aura about him...

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: ...And on top of that, the kind of medicine practiced in the Chenyu Vale tradition goes against the natural order of things.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...In what way?

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Don't know. My grandpa didn't know the specifics, and you've seen how wary Baizhu is around me. He'd never tell me anything...

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: But even that says to me that he definitely has something to hide.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: One thing I do know about Baizhu is that he's obsessed with the idea of immortality... But whether that has anything to do with what he's hiding is hard to say.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Immortality...?)

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Anyway, so I will be sticking around here for now to keep a close eye on the situation. Maybe tomorrow, I'll finally figure out what he's up to...

dialogues.speaker: Qiqi
dialogues.text: His family. We have to find them.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, Paimon doesn't think we've seen this side of you. But there's no need to thank us! You've helped us out before.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So. What are the next steps?

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: The poison in Jialiang's system must have accumulated over a prolonged period. I think I should pay a visit to their family home, and look for clues as to how he might have been exposed to it.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Do you know where his house is?

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: Yes. I asked Ayu this morning before you arrived. He told me that his family lives in a secluded spot to the west of Qingce Village.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: Let's head there together once I've asked Gui and Qiqi to look after the pharmacy.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: ...As well as investigating Jialiang's exposure to the poison, we should also keep an eye out for Ayu's missing mother... my fellow disciple, Jiangli.

dialogues.speaker: Ayu
dialogues.text: Dad!

dialogues.speaker: Jialiang
dialogues.text: Huh... Ayu!

dialogues.speaker: Ayu
dialogues.text: Dad! You remember me!

dialogues.speaker: Jialiang
dialogues.text: Yes, I remember now! Oh, Ayu, I'm so sorry, you must have been worried sick... Has your mom shown up yet? She's... been gone for a while, hasn't she?

dialogues.speaker: Ayu
dialogues.text: Don't worry, Dad! I got the Adventurers' Guild to help us look for her. And Dr. Baizhu's gonna help too! Right now, all you need to do is concentrate on getting better!

dialogues.speaker: Jialiang
dialogues.text: Great, that's wonderful... I can't thank you enough, Dr. Baizhu.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: My pleasure, really. It's the least I can do to honor my late master's dying wish. If anything, I should be apologizing to you for not making the time to visit in all these years.

dialogues.speaker: Jialiang
dialogues.text: Hah, not at all, Dr. Baizhu. It's only because Jiangli... hmm... What was her reason again...

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: ...You're still in the early stages of recovery, so you'll need to take it easy for a while. Take it slowly, and try not to over-exert yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Changsheng
dialogues.text: I suggest you stay at Bubu Pharmacy and rest for at least the next few days.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: Director Hu, do you have any further reservations about Jialiang's condition?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: ...Hmm, it seems like the evil presence is gone after all. You really did manage to suppress it, huh...

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: ...But how did you accomplish this in a single night?

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: Hahaha, that would be a trade secret, I'm afraid. If that gives you any cause for concern, you may continue to monitor Jialiang for as long as you wish.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: Though I regret to say that Bubu Pharmacy cannot offer to reimburse Wangsheng Funeral Parlor for any revenue lost in the meantime.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: ...Oh, come on, Baizhu. I'm not THAT unreasonable.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Baizhu looks a little worse for wear...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Something's wrong.)

dialogues.speaker: Changsheng
dialogues.text: Ahhhhh — I've been stuck indoors for too long. Baizhu, take me outside for some air, or I'm going to suffocate!

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: Ah yes, of course... Everyone, please excuse Changsheng and myself for a moment.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: ... *cough* *cough*

dialogues.speaker: Changsheng
dialogues.text: Suffering now, are we? Did you seriously expect to cover it up just by putting on a brave face and ignoring it? If it weren't for my quick thinking, they'd all have seen the sorry state you're in by now.

dialogues.speaker: Changsheng
dialogues.text: But in any case, why must you keep this a secret from everybody? You should at least share your secret with one person you trust...

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: Who's there?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aaaah!!!!

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: ...Why did you follow us here?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I thought you were looking a little unwell...

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: Oh, hehe, it's nothing. I just needed to get some air... *cough*

response.speaker: Changsheng
response.text: What did I JUST say about putting on a brave face? Tsk...

response.speaker: Changsheng
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, the truth is... Baizhu did not cure Jialiang's illness.

response.speaker: Changsheng
response.text: Instead, he transferred some of his own life force to his patient to temporarily subdue the poison in his system.

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: *sigh*

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Baizhu... Can you please explain all of this?

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: ...My predecessors in medicine forged a contract with Changsheng. Every successor to this contract is able to use Changsheng's secret art to treat patients.

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: I believe the irregularities with Jialiang's heart meridian were likely caused by a poison concocted using god remains as a key ingredient.

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: The poison has not been purged from Jialiang's system. Rather, I infused him with some of my own life force using Changsheng as the delivery medium. This will suppress the poison's effects for a limited time.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Changsheng... You can do that? Paimon always thought you were just Baizhu's strange choice of a necklace...

response.speaker: Changsheng
response.text: Hey! I'll have you know that I commanded the respect of even the adepti back in Chenyu Vale. If anything, he is my mannequin!

response.speaker: Changsheng
response.text: I was treating patients with Baizhu's master's master long before he ever set eyes on his first medical text!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa... Guess you shouldn't judge a snake by its skin.

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: Please, that's enough... *cough* *cough*

choices.text: You're looking even worse now than before...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait a sec... Hu Tao was saying that the branch of medicine you studied uses some pretty dubious methods... So when you transfer your life force, does that mean you're actually damaging your own body?

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: Hardly. Changsheng helps to keep my qi in balance, so there is no great harm done...

response.speaker: Changsheng
response.text: ...Still, Baizhu's life force is not unlimited. We must find a way to neutralize the poison in Jialiang's body, and soon.

response.speaker: Changsheng
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, would you lend this dummy a hand? He needs someone checking up on him, or he'll exhaust himself trying to accomplish everything on his own...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Go on, Baizhu. Let us help you.

response.speaker: Changsheng
response.text: ...Baizhu, don't you think you should seize this opportunity? You cannot expect to hide this from everyone for your entire life. Time will see that all secrets surface eventually.

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: *sigh*... "Entire life"...

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: #...Thank you, {NICKNAME} and Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, Paimon doesn't think we've seen this side of you before.

dialogues.speaker: Cai Xun
dialogues.text: I'm afraid we have to stay at our posts, so we won't be able to join you on the search.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Baizhu and Changsheng are treating Jialiang right now... I should come back tomorrow.)

dialogues.speaker: Ayu
dialogues.text: Mr. Gui, I wanna go to the Adventurers' Guild and get them to help look for my mom. Should I take anything with me?

dialogues.speaker: Herbalist Gui
dialogues.text: Hmm... You'll need enough cash to pay their fees, and there'll be some paperwork to fill out... I can come with you if you'd like?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, these two are hard at work... We probably shouldn't disturb them.

dialogues.speaker: Qiqi
dialogues.text: Jiangli... Master... Dr. Baizhu has never mentioned them before...

dialogues.speaker: Qiqi
dialogues.text: But more importantly... Is you-know-who gone yet?

dialogues.speaker: Qiqi
dialogues.text: Ohhh... I need to find a better hiding place...

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Oh, while you're here — have either of you seen Qiqi around?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: It's not every day I get to infiltrate Baizhu's lair. But alas, I didn't catch a single glimpse of her anywhere...

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Aha! What if... Baizhu knew I'd be on the lookout for her, and hid her away in advance?

dialogues.speaker: Cai Le
dialogues.text: We'll update our superiors on the situation and see if they can assign anyone else to help.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: The group returns to the back room at Bubu Pharmacy...

dialogues.speaker: Ayu
dialogues.text: Daaaaad!

dialogues.speaker: Ayu
dialogues.text: Daaaaaaad...! Can you hear me...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Look, there's somebody over there!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whew... After all that, it seems like we have more questions than answers!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Never mind. We'll just have to ask Baizhu himself about all of this tomorrow!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's a new day! Let's go back to Bubu Pharmacy and check out how Jialiang is doing!
